But I'd like to point out, the Urban Dictionary Definition of "Otaku" is completely wrong. What it describes Otakus as is actually what another type of people are, called "Hikikomoris".

Otaku is an overtly negative term in Japan to describe an addiction to something that is so strong that it is considered to be unhealthy for that person. Basically, it's an insult. That term is misused a lot in the Western Hemisphere to describe huge anime fans, when that's not even close to what it actually means.

Take myself, for examplle. I am what you call, a Gundam Otaku. My love of the anime series, Mobile Suit Gundam, has far passed the point of beiing unhealthy for myself. I know pretty much every single little aching detail about pretty much everything and anything Gundam, so much to the point where I memorized what is said in multiple episodes practically Word for Word.

Now as for the original question in place here, I think Weaboos, NEETs, Hikikomoris, and Otakus seriously need to get a reality check and get back into the real world and maybe get some counseling done on them. The thing is, this is actually a very big problem in Japan even now. A lot of Japan's Youth have been engaging in way too much escapism to the point where they literally become hermits, locked away in their own fantasies going on in their mind, and lose grip on reality.

But if I may just point out, asking someone to not reply in an offensive tone when the terms "Weeaboo" and "Otaku" are both Offensive and Insulting Terms to call people.....isn't that like a contradiction???? O_o

As a self-proclaimed weeabo/otaku, let me speak in our defense. Some of us, anyway.

Anime and Manga are a medium just like any other. There's stuff of every genre imaginable, for every demographic imaginable. It has a stigma in the west of being either a DBZ clone, a Sailor Moon clone, a Pokemon clone or porn, but this isn't even remotely true. I mean sure, there's plenty of that stuff, but there's plenty of everything else as well. I would bet that everyone in this thread could find some Anime or Manga that they enjoyed at least to some degree.

But not only is there the stigma I spoke of, but the more vocal of weeaboos/otaku can be severely obnoxious. These Naruto-Headband-Wearing weirdos do NOT represent otaku as a whole, they're just the loudest of us. And the fact is, that people who are serious otaku - who really, really get into the hobby, at least in the west, are often very moderate people who absolutely can't stand these "Narutard" types. We realize that these people make us look bad, and even worse, they make the hobby we love look bad, and it puts off other people from potentially enjoying it too.

Some of the more serious otaku can be pretty damn weird, but a lot of us keep our obsession to ourselves and our close friends. I know I've watched some shit that would probably make you want to splash me with holy water and flee, but I don't expect you to watch shit like that. But the more obnoxious otaku aren't like that. They're the ones that will shout in your face about how "ANIME IS THE SUPERIOR MEDIUM AND YOU JUST DON'T UNDERSTAND HOW EPIC AND DEEP ATTACK ON TITAN IS!!" and not understand that people have different types of media that they enjoy. They annoy us just as much as they annoy you.

So I personally say, give Anime a shot. If you like watching movies or TV shows at all, there is almost certainly something that will tickle your fancy. And no, it's not fucking Attack on Titan.

Honestly, do whatever you want. If it makes you happy, go for it. It doesn't really effect me. I even like some anime, and Japanese food is good.. but I think having any kind of cultural obsession can be unhealthy, mentally and socially.
